title: Choose the world your heroes live in
question: The roll dealt the Reading Table. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Each sketch is the return screen: what a player sees coming back after a night of duels.

options.label: The Reading Table
options.lineage: Tarot de Marseille decks laid on a reading cloth
options.thesis: Every duel is two cards laid face-down at once and turned together: upright keeps faith, reversed betrays.
options.viewport: The night's readings lie face-down in a spread across the cloth; your hero's card sits at the head; the candle that burned while you were away holds your haul; one action lays tonight's spread.
options.risk: Tarot carries fortune-telling connotations and is familiar from Persona-style arcana systems; it can read mystical before competitive.

raised.raise: Collections (arcana, badges) pack edge to edge as stamp-sized cards with hand-marked state, never sparse tiles.
Every hero and duel state is materially distinct: resting, laid, turned, scored, forfeited.
After a turn, the road not taken shows as a faint ghost card with what the other choice would have scored.
Results read in one ordered row, gravity-sorted by fortune, so the best and worst of the night are found without reading.
Recency is ink density: the newest reading is printed darkest, older ones fade toward the stock.

options.label: Heel Turn
options.thesis: Betrayal is a heel turn and trust is a handshake in the ring: every hero is a wrestler with a gimmick, every night a printed card.
options.viewport: Last night's card printed as a poster: your wrestler's matches listed with handshake or heel-turn stamps, the gym purse waiting, tonight's match to book.
options.risk: Loud wrestling camp can tip toward toy-like, and kayfabe reads strongest to US/Mexican audiences rather than globally.

options.label: The Tear-off
options.thesis: Coming back means tearing leaves: every session you missed is a dated leaf on the pad, torn away one by one to reveal how your hero fared.
options.viewport: Your hero's plate fills the top sheet with its name in gold script; below, a pad of missed sittings waits to be torn.
options.case: Fuses cleanly for the return screen (time is the one axis, tearing is the reveal); loses on the tinkerer surfaces and wants a painted plate the no-AI-image rule forces into code.
options.risk: The painted plate must be drawn in code, and a calendar has little to say about the tower or the build.

options.label: Convention Catalog
options.thesis: Heroes as stamp-sized circle entries in a packed hall grid.
options.viewport: A dense numbered grid of hero thumbnails with a hall map.
options.case: Loses both axes: players don't identify with a fan-convention catalog, and duels don't map to tables.
options.kept: Density courage: collections packed edge to edge with hand-marked state.

options.label: Tension Column
options.thesis: Trust as tension cords between heroes.
options.case: Loses both axes: abstract engineering, no hero to raise.
options.kept: Distinct states for every member: slack, balanced, stressed, failed.

options.label: Collision Display
options.thesis: Each duel frozen as a collision event with tracks.
options.viewport: Concentric rings with the night's duels as tracks.
options.case: Loses both axes and lands in the crypto-dashboard look you ruled out.
options.kept: Competing outcomes overlaid as ghosts: the road not taken.

options.label: Glaze Shelf
options.lineage: kiln shelves of glaze test cups
options.thesis: Heroes as glaze samples running under heat.
options.viewport: A shelf row of fired samples.
options.case: Loses both axes: no conflict, no hero.
options.kept: One gravity-ordered row so outcomes read by position.

options.label: Ink Basin
options.viewport: A marbled basin of the night's encounters.
options.case: Loses both axes: ambient, not competitive.
options.kept: Recency as ink density: newest darkest.

canonCard.label: The genre standard
canonCard.thesis: The AFK-RPG gacha home, played straight at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Hero portrait center stage in a gilded frame, resources across the top, the idle chest glowing, event banners, five-tab bottom bar.
canonCard.risk: Interchangeable with every game in the genre by design.
